description: How the crypto exchange world went from wild growth to a house-of-cards collapse: Binance's dominance, Coinbase's IPO peak-and-slide, Kraken's steady private-value run, and FTX's explosive rise to zero (Nov 2022). Market-value-style comparison (Billions USD) showing one empire erupt while another implodes.
youtube_description:
Short version: this chart race tracks the implied market value of the top crypto exchanges from the early pre-exchange years up through 2026. Watch Binance erupt into the dominant juggernaut, Coinbase spike at its 2021 direct listing then fall with the crypto winter, Kraken hold steady as a high-valued private player, and FTX shoot up to a reported ~$32B private valuation before collapsing to near-zero in November 2022.

Why this matters: the exchange world powered crypto's liquidity — and when one of the giants failed it wiped out trust, capital, and billions overnight. This visualization uses public market caps (Coinbase) and commonly reported private valuations/enterprise-value proxies (Binance, Kraken, FTX) to tell the dramatic story.

If you want more deep-dives like this (sources, charts, and an animation pack), like & subscribe and drop a comment on what to compare next.

Sources referenced in research: Coinbase direct-listing market cap (Apr 2021), FTX private valuation peak reported mid‑2021 (~$32B) and the FTX collapse in Nov 2022, Kraken private funding rounds valuing it near ~$10B in early 2022, plus public reporting on Binance's rapid growth and regulatory scrutiny.

Watch the annotations in the video for dates & events. Smash that like button if the FTX spike-and-collapse shocks you. Subscribe for weekly chart races.
